name: Dust & Frequency
subcategory: the Gray Zone culture and music broadcast
creator: Originated by Amara Johanssen-Diallo; now collectively maintained
description: A beloved underground broadcast running since 2195, Dust & Frequency airs a mix of live music, oral storytelling, neighborhood news, and cultural programming made by and for the Gray Zone communities, transmitted on salvaged audio hardware and low-bandwidth neural bleed. Its signature segment, 'The Mouth,' features anonymous callers describing daily life in the Gray Zone in unedited, unmoderated testimony that has become a primary oral history archive of Tier 1 existence. The show runs whenever its rotating volunteer hosts can get air — sometimes nightly, sometimes after a week of silence.
medium: legacy audio (primary), low-bandwidth neural bleed, physical cassette distribution
cultural_impact: Dust & Frequency has created a distributed oral archive of the Gray Zone life that historians, underground journalists, and human rights researchers quietly access as a primary source; its cassette releases are traded across all tiers as cultural artifacts.
controversy: In 2211, a Dust & Frequency episode featured an anonymous testimony that named a HelixCorp mid-level manager by full name in connection with a protection racket; the named individual filed a Defamation and Unauthorized Broadcast complaint. The episode remains in circulation on physical cassette.
story_hooks: The 'Mouth' segment receives a testimony that contains technical details about an upcoming corponation operation that no civilian should know — and now the entire broadcast network is in danger from whoever wants that information suppressed.
Amara Johanssen-Diallo's original recordings from 2195-2199 are missing from the archive; someone has them, and whether they want to preserve or destroy the record is unclear.
A Tier 4 music label wants to officially release a Dust & Frequency compilation — the collective is divided between those who see it as legitimization and those who see it as co-optation.
